title: NorthStar Health integration checkpoints — weekly sync
summary: Weekly sync focusing on production-ready network handoffs, fallback model routing, and performance regression observed in staging after quantized model rollout.
content:
Attendees: Asha (SE lead), Ethan (FieldEng), Maya (ProServices PM), Diego (SRE), Priya (Security eng), Claire (NorthStar technical lead - remote)

Meeting purpose: triage outstanding integration items for NorthStar Health (NSH), align on next steps for VPC peering and private deployment options, and decide rollback vs. roll-forward for the quantized model experiment that caused higher tail latency in staging.

High-level status
- Onboarding phase: late technical validation. Business onboarding and contracts signed; Dedicated capacity reservation done (reserve pool id: dp-nsh-07). Target go-live window: 2027-05-06 — still achievable if major blockers cleared by 2027-04-28.
- Workstream split: Network & Security (Priya + NSH infra), Model serving (Asha + Diego), Observability & SLOs (Ethan + SRE), Runbooks & Handoffs (Maya + Solutions docs).

Recent progress since last sync
- VPC peering proof-of-concept completed in staging: NSH accepted route tables and test traffic over BGP. Latency baseline for echo tests: 6–9 ms RTT to the dedicated control plane in us-west-2.
- Private control plane container deployed in NSH dev VPC; initial health checks pass. KMS integration handshake complete with test key (not production key yet).
- Model variant matrix updated: added q4_8bit_fp16 fallback for the medical-NL-large model to ensure deterministic inference when the quantized path degrades.
- Observability: tracing headers propagated end-to-end; token-level cost traces visible in staging console. Synthetic prompt suite run after the quantized rollout surfaced elevated p95 generation latency for sequences >512 tokens.

Issues surfaced (blockers)
1) Quantized model p95 tail latency regression (staging)
   - Symptoms: after switching traffic to q4_8bit quantized variant in staging, p95 increased from 210 ms to ~470 ms for prompts with longer context (>512). p50 unchanged.
   - Root-candidate: kernel selection path for 2048-token attention windows falling back to slower execution kernel; quantized matmul path hitting a cache alignment boundary on A100s under high concurrency.
   - Impact: risk of missing customer latency SLO of 350 ms for the 'interactive note drafting' flow.
   - Temporary mitigation: enable auto-fallback routing by sequence-length policy to non-quantized variant for requests with predicted seq_len > 600 (deployed as a routing rule in staging).
   - Decision needed: rollback quantized rollout or change serving configuration and re-run load test.

2) VPC peering intermittent SYN retransmits
   - Symptoms: under burst egress (~100 concurrent control-plane connections) we see TCP retransmits between NSH VPC and our control plane. Packet captures show occasional MSS mismatch on the path.
   - Root-candidate: MTU settings inconsistently set across customer firewall appliance + cloud transit. NSH firewall vendor expects 1460 but AWS path is 1500.
   - Mitigation: SRE recommended enabling MSS clamping on the customer firewall; Diego and NSH infra will validate.
   - Risk: control plane reconnections could cause brief API timeouts; mitigation required before go-live.

3) Audit log cadence for Private deployment
   - Ask from NSH compliance: 90-day immutable audit retention and HSM signing for critical actions. Current private build supports configurable retention but not HSM-signed immutable logs.
   - Action: Security to scope HSM integration and legal to confirm acceptable retention SLA. Expect scoping doc by 2027-04-26.

Decisions and tradeoffs discussed
- Quantized rollout: group agreed to avoid full rollback. Instead, we will patch the runtime kernel selection to use sequence-length hinting earlier in the pipeline, enable the sequence-based fallback rule (seq_len > 600), and re-run the synthetic load + regression suite by 2027-04-24. If p95 remains >350 ms, we will perform a rollback no later than 2027-04-26.
- VPC: require NSH infra to enable MSS clamping and validate with pressure tests. If retransmits persist after firewall change, we will escalate to vendor support and temporarily route control-plane traffic via our us-east-1 mirror control plane until resolved.

Action items (owners and ETA)
- Asha: draft kernel-selection patch PR for serving runtime that checks predicted sequence-length earlier; PR by 2027-04-23 EOD. Linked PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/417 (WIP).
- Diego: schedule and run pressure test for the VPC peering after NSH enables MSS clamp; test window 2027-04-23 10:00–11:30 PT. Report results in ticket JIRA-INT-3214.
- Priya: produce HSM integration scope doc and security review checklist for immutable audit logging; due 2027-04-26.
- Ethan: update the synthetic prompt suite to include 1,000 multi-turn sessions with variable context lengths (extend to 2,048 tokens) and run nightly until 2027-04-29; share results to #se-proservices-alerts channel.
- Maya: finalize the handoff runbook with post-deploy rollback steps and support rotation schedule; publish runbook draft to confluence by 2027-04-24.
- Claire (NSH): enable MSS clamping on perimeter firewall and confirm backchannel when done; ETA 2027-04-23.

Risks & contingencies
- If kernel patch cannot be delivered without risky change to runtime scheduling, fallback plan is a targeted rollback of quantized variants for NSH only (causing ~18% cost delta). Sales and customer success have been pre-briefed on possible cost impact.
- HSM timeline slips could delay privacy attestation; we may need to offer additional contractual mitigations (audit export with customer-managed KMS) as a stopgap.
- If VPC issues persist beyond 2027-04-26, recommend delaying go-live by one sprint (2 weeks) — communicate to NSH leadership.

Notes from customer (Claire)
- NSH engineering is comfortable with the seq_len fallback plan but emphasized zero-tolerance for degraded availability during clinical triage hours (08:00–20:00 ET). They asked for a hard SLO blackout-window in the first two weeks post launch where any incident must trigger immediate on-call paging to the NSH ops pager in addition to our on-call.
- Claire also requested example payloads for end-to-end compliance testing (we will deliver sample sanitized events by 2027-04-23).

Parking lot (deferred items)
- On-prem installer packaging for air-gapped installs (customer asked; deprioritize until NSH requests).
- Cost-optimization playbook for their low-volume nightly batch job (follow-up in Q3).

Next sync
- Weekly cadence retained. Next touchpoint: 2027-04-26 09:30 PT (short triage focused on kernel patch results and MSS clamp validation). If kernel patch greenlights earlier, we'll switch to an emergency-only cadence.

Appendix: quick logs and metrics (staging)
- Baseline p50/p95 (non-quantized): 180 ms / 210 ms
- After quantized rollout (staging): 200 ms / 470 ms
- Current routing mitigation estimate: expected p95 ~ 260–300 ms for traffic mix with fallback rule
- Control-plane RTT to us-west-2: 6–9 ms (echo), typical TLS handshake 45–60 ms under cold connections

End of notes.
